opti-1: Long ago, parks began sending rangers to teach visitors about nature.
opti-2: In 1920, scientists started free nature walks in Yosemite.
opti-3: Today, exhibits use real photos, models, and just a few words.
opti-4: Rangers give short talks, so visitors can understand in minutes.
opti-5: Every sign, talk, and slide starts with real evidence.
opti-6: How do you turn scientific research into something other people can actually understand?
32-02-welcome: Our film starts with park rangers from 100 years ago. First, inspect a mystery made of glass.
32-02-lesson: Today you're a science communicator. Follow park science to visitors, run the Visitor Test, then hunt for the criteria.
32-02-check: Three quick questions. It's not graded. It's just for you, so give each one your best try.
32-02-assign: Time to build! Plan in Part A, then make your real slides in the Park Slide Studio and present them.
how-32-02-specimen: Press Inspect specimen. Move the magnifying lens over the slide, then tap three things you notice.
how-32-02-compare: Put the visitor with two minutes under one tray and the reader with lots of time under the other: drag them, or tap one, then a tray. Press Start reading. Then swap.
how-32-02-wall: First, make a prediction. Then brush the glowing exhibit: drag across it (or tap it again and again) until the photo shows.
how-32-02-det: Pick three cards, one at a time. Tap what you see, then name the criterion it fits. Decide if the slide's sentence is strong evidence, and see the answer.
how-32-02-partc: Pick your park. Build six slides, one for each criterion. Practice with the two-minute timer. Then make your video, or download your slides, and upload the file to Canvas.
studio-howto-01: Have you ever made a presentation? Here's how to build yours in the Park Slide Studio.
studio-howto-02: A presentation is a few slides you show while you talk. Each slide has one big idea, one picture, and a few words.
studio-howto-03: Look at these two slides. The first one is short, with a real photo and a fact. The second one has too many words for a visitor.
studio-howto-04: Press Got it, then pick your park.
studio-howto-05: Your six slides are up here, one for each criterion.
studio-howto-06: Need facts? Each slide has Field Notes with true facts about your park. Pick one, and write it in your own words.
studio-howto-07: Start with slide one. Not sure how to begin? Press Use a sentence starter, then finish the sentence.
studio-howto-08: Watch the word counter. Keep each slide between five and thirty words.
studio-howto-09: Now pick a real photo. Tap one, and it jumps onto your slide.
studio-howto-10: These three checks turn green when your slide is strong: the right number of words, a picture, and a specific detail.
studio-howto-11: Want your visitor to hear you? Press Record my voice, talk, then press Stop. Your voice goes inside your slides.
studio-howto-12: On the food web slide, pick a plant, an animal that eats it, and an animal that eats that one.
studio-howto-13: When every circle at the top is lit, your slides meet all six criteria.
studio-howto-14: Press Present to practice out loud. You have two minutes, so talk about each slide for about twenty seconds.
studio-howto-15: Last, press Make my video. Your slides and your voice turn into a video. Upload it to Canvas. You did it, presenter!
